e: From Spanish xoconostle, from Classical Nahuatl xoconōchtli (“sour prickly-pear”).
From Nahuatl xocomecatl (“grapevine”) (alluding to its appearance as a set of green spherules), and -ite.
From Nahuatl xōchinacaztli (“ear-flower”), from xōchitl (“flower”). So called because it somewhat resembles an ear.
